title: World-building atlas
usage: Reference only; overall narrative and later phases
analysis: A text-heavy collage with orbital planet, three biomes, ensemble portraits, costume silhouettes, foods, gold framing and crisis thumbnails. Black, bronze, cyan and violet bind the composition. Cinematic faces mix with infographic graphics; do not place this collage into a scene. Its names are superseded by LEXORYN canon. Vehicles, architecture and clothing are tiny concept cues, not production assets.

title: Capital cloud city
usage: Phase 1: atmospheric entry and Velair Prime reveal
analysis: Tapered graphite megatowers, circular landing decks, amber-lit avenues and dense facades rise through cream cloud layers. Low golden sunlight creates long shadows and layered haze. Small dark flying craft establish scale. No visible character or costume detail. The giant crescent and orb belong to this artwork only; do not reproduce them as the original planet exterior.

title: Orbital command deck
usage: Later: orbital intelligence archive; Phase 1 interface direction
analysis: Ribbed dark metal cockpit, panoramic windows, amber inset light strips, cyan holographic nodes and a round projected command table. Two human operators in subdued dark uniforms provide scale. Planet outside resembles Earth; keep the photo out of the opening exterior. No foreground vehicle exterior. Translate the restrained cyan/amber instrument language into usable HTML controls.

title: Storm spire
analysis: A needle-like dark tower under immense storm clouds, cyan lightning to the left and hot amber electrical fractures to the right. Fine urban details and wet reflective light imply scale. No readable people or transport. At 292 × 232 this is a thumbnail: never upscale for a hero.

title: Colossal reactor gate
analysis: A monumental annular machine dominates a symmetrical canyon complex, with nested machined rings and dense radial mechanisms. White-gold reactor emission bounces off bronze metal and a wet, dark foreground. Small silhouetted visitors wear long dark utilitarian clothing. Storm-blue sky and stony flanks anchor the heat. Strong clean environment plate at its native wide ratio.

title: Defense commander
usage: Later: General Kaor character direction and portrait
analysis: Bald, muscular male figure with a trimmed goatee and stern frontal gaze. Articulated charcoal/gunmetal armor, brushed silver plates, black flexible underlayers and sparse cyan seams. Warm corridor bars and cold stellar backlight shape the face and shoulders. Industrial spacecraft framing, no landscape or vehicle exterior. Use this portrait consistently; do not substitute unrelated faces. No footwear is visible.

title: Concord market
analysis: Crowded, layered circular bazaar with brass hanging lamps, metallic ducts, ochre produce and shafts of dusty daylight. Humanoid alien traders have sculpted elongated heads, olive-gold skin/helmets and embroidered ochre, rust and teal robes. Ornamental cuffs and textiles contrast hard metal. A small suspended luminous globe is a prop, not the planet exterior. No vehicles or clearly visible footwear.

title: Sky bike at sunset
usage: Later: transport / Kito Ren; vehicle design direction in Phase 1
analysis: Aerodynamic charcoal and silver flying motorcycle with cyan propulsion and circular wheel assemblies. A rider wears a fitted protective suit, gloves and a closed red-black helmet; visible boots are integrated into the riding silhouette. Orange-pink sunset and distant hover traffic create speed and scale over a tall city. More saturated and polished than the main plates; present separately rather than compositing it into the gold city.

title: Orbital hangar
usage: Phase 1: arrival dossier / capital transport detail
analysis: Immense ribbed steel hangar, angular roof supports, segmented reflective floor and hazy white daylight. Rounded silver shuttle fuselages with dark cockpit glass, recessed engines and amber running lights hover at multiple depths. Small suited crew wear dark utility uniforms and boots. Cool gray materials and restrained gold illumination match the capital industrial language.

title: Cryonth energy rupture
usage: Later: crisis / Cryonth event; exterior material direction only
analysis: A giant dark cracked sphere splits around a violent cyan energy column above a cold reflective plain. Jagged rock, ice-like textures, blue mist and tiny orange fissures convey instability. No people, clothing or vehicles. A surreal ground-level event, not an orbital planet photo: reserve the plate for a later crisis sequence. Borrow only dark mineral scale and emissive fracture restraint for the original mesh.

title: Floating Concord sanctum
analysis: Golden domes, carved sandstone/bronze walls, colonnades and sweeping bridges stand on suspended rock-like foundations over thick white clouds. Warm sidelight and peach atmospheric perspective create depth. Thin waterfalls and distant dark flyers suggest living scale. No readable character costumes. Ceremonial architecture complements rather than replaces the modern capital skyline.

title: Convergence hall
analysis: Symmetric monumental gold ring apparatus above stepped reflective terraces. Cyan-white energy inscriptions and fine hanging gold rods frame the apparatus. Ranks of small robed citizens flank a central lone figure, with ceremonial dark crimson/bronze garments. Mountains and diffuse warm sky set exterior scale. No transport. Preserve this ceremonial visual vocabulary for the Night of Convergence.

title: Biosphere monitoring room
analysis: Circular industrial room in cyan and orange with two uniformed operators, radial structural ribs and bright inset lamps. Large round dashboards show Earth continents and malformed generated labels. Useful for color, holographic display hierarchy and practical operator clothing, but unsuitable as a clean LEXORYN scene because its embedded text and geography conflict with the project.

title: Character triptych
usage: Reference only: later costume and accessory development
analysis: Three unrelated portrait treatments: left, a realistic braided woman with gold ear devices, forehead jewel and luminous cyan chest ornament; center, an older realistic man with transparent cyan smart glasses and a dark circuit-embroidered coat; right, a stylized violet armored fantasy woman with an elaborate horned crown. Black rounded card edges and a bookmark overlay are baked in. Keep the first two as accessory/material direction; exclude the right-hand cartoon/fantasy treatment from final realism. No full footwear, architecture or vehicles.

title: Engineered mineral world
usage: Reference only: original 3D exterior materials and scale
analysis: An immense dark mineral sphere is engraved with concentric engineered cavities and sparse hot amber seams. A hard sunrise creates a bright gold rim and cyan lens streak over a rocky canyon. Broken rock and distant moons build scale; no visible people, costumes or vehicles. This is a surreal ground-level composition, not a physically literal orbital view. Borrow worn obsidian surfaces, ancient engineering, silhouette and rim lighting; never substitute this flat image for the real 3D planet.

title: Concord orbital station
usage: Phase 1: orbital station geometry direction; approved archive plate
analysis: An intricate ring station surrounds an axial docking complex, with lattice spokes, layered silver panels, bronze solar arrays, cyan machinery and amber interior docks. A heavy shuttle approaches while smaller craft provide scale. Starfield and warm planetary limb establish strong perspective and occlusion. No readable characters. Use this as the production-design anchor for real 3D ring geometry rather than a billboard station.

title: Velair Prime aerial district
usage: Phase 1: wide city reveal and observation-platform outlook
analysis: Dense black-titanium and bronze towers blend carved domed civic silhouettes with cyan luminous facade channels. Elevated rails, bridges and bright road lanes cross at multiple depths; small transit vehicles, markets and warm shop lights establish a lived-in capital. Late amber sunlight and blue haze separate the distant skyline. No distinguishable faces or costume details. The line of tall stabilizer-like towers and monumental crowned civic buildings define the capital design language.

title: Meridia storm corridor cockpit
usage: Phase 1: entry art direction; later route/transport archive plate
analysis: First-person vehicle cockpit looks through rain-beaded glazing toward dark volcanic ridges, a rough water corridor and a single amber lightning strike. Cool cyan-gray fog contrasts orange analog instrument glow. A pilot wears weathered black gloves and rust-orange technical sleeves; no face or footwear is visible. Thick canopy struts and practical illuminated switches support believable vehicle construction. The composition is a low-altitude flight reference, not cloud-only imagery; avoid claiming a volumetric simulation from this still.
